accepted_change.name: prefer-dispatch
accepted_change.description: When READY work and retrieved completions coexist, refill free Worker slots before returning the completion to the workflow reactor.
accepted_change.scope: DataVine runtime tuning only; generic TaskVine keeps its default policy.

rejected_change.name: direct-poll-worker-pointer
rejected_change.note: Status CPU fell, but end-to-end throughput did not; source was restored.

command_no_output.interpretation: Two-run process-creation-dominated guard; no claimed speedup.

correctness_fix.name: function-call-output-materialization
correctness_fix.description: Materialize DataVine FunctionCall output from Worker memory into its declared sandbox output before Agent commit.
correctness_fix.failure_before: OUTPUT_MISSING for the first dependent task output
correctness_fix.coverage: native-function-output regression plus the exact 20000-task layered DAG

conclusion: The local independent-task ceiling was primarily completion-to-refill latency, not DataVine completion bookkeeping. Prefer-dispatch removes most scheduler delay without batching or changing ownership; data-heavy and bulk guards remain stable.
